unharnessed.meaning: Every point survives: the compliance burden, contractor or web team, FedRAMP JAB, preview URLs and signoff, static over CMS, no PHP or Apache / IIS, one file server not dozens, GitHub editor, Amazon S3 pay-for-use, customisation. "knock up a website" makes "create" sound a bit slapdash.
unharnessed.sense: Mostly fits: "getting the security and privacy compliance sorted", "compliance grunt work", "fewer weak spots", "dead easy". "get the tick-off on content updates" strains: the idiom is the tick of approval, and "tick-off" suggests a telling-off. "knock up a website" also has an unwanted reading.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural Australian workplace voice: "chances are you've been handed what looks like a simple job", "Static websites have a few things going for them". "tick-off" is the one off idiom; "Fully customizable" keeps the US spelling.
unharnessed.register: Level 3: a light, conversational Aussie retelling of the marketing page without becoming slangy; no swearing.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the helpful, persuasive government-product tone.
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly; the doubled "Steering clear of a traditional CMS means steering clear of headaches" is a deliberate echo of the original.
unharnessed.variety: Varied: "knock up", "sorted", "grunt work", "know-how", "checked off", "tick-off", "headaches", "weak spots", "dead easy".
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the cloud.gov Pages explainer, headings and bullets intact.

engine.meaning: Almost all of the original survives verbatim; two swaps distort it: "Pages knocks together out draft updates" and "Static sites can be used to knock together many different types of sites" suggest slapdash building.
engine.sense: Wrong-sense or strained swaps: "knock together" (cobble up roughly) for "build", twice; "properly easy" for "very easy".
engine.authenticity: Mechanical swaps into untouched US marketing prose: "Pages knocks together out draft updates to your site", "It’s properly easy to host".
engine.register: Far under level 3: the original verbatim apart from three swaps and "organisation".
engine.tone: Original tone kept, since the text is.
engine.flow: Broken where it changes anything: "Pages knocks together out draft updates".
engine.essence: Recognisably the original page, barely changed.

yarn.meaning: Every point survives, close to the original: "the security and privacy compliance sorted so you can launch the actual website and keep it running", "one simple static file server or service, not dozens".
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "get the tick of approval on content updates", "sorted", "know-how", "dead easy", "headaches", "pile extra load on".
yarn.authenticity: Natural Australian workplace English: "chances are you’ve been handed what looks like a simple job", "Fully customisable", "organisation".
yarn.register: Level 3, on the light side: a natural Aussie register with a few idioms; stretches stay close to the original ("So the whole website is easier to maintain and has fewer vulnerabilities.").
yarn.variety: Varied, nothing leaned on: "sorted", "looks after", "know-how", "count on", "tick of approval", "steering clear", "dead easy", "make the most of".

'Knock up' (make quickly) is Australian, but suggests a rough job and has an unwanted second reading.
US spelling kept in the heading while 'organisation' is localised.
